newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee rebounds on NY, Brazil weather news.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee rebounds on NY, Brazil weather news.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures pared losses to close with slight gains on Wednesday on the back of New York's brief rise following forecasts of possible cold in Brazil coffee districts late next week.
But the market still closed a shade lower as profit-taking set in at the highs and after several other forecasters played down the possibility of a frost.
September finished $2 up at $1,670 per tonne, the day's high, after a low of $1,640. New York's September raced to a high of 198 cents a lb before trading 7.10 up at 196 at 1620 GMT.
Values were earlier pressured by Far East hedge selling.
Indonesian sellers were making a comeback, selling into any price rise after much hesitation in the past weeks. The September futures prices had risen by some $193 in a week.
New York's bullish mood was spurred by extended Brazilian weather outlook which predicted colder temperatures in the coffee belt during the weekend of August 9.
U.S. weather forecaster Cropcast said long-range guidance models showed Brazil's coffee belt could see colder temperatures late next week with a 15 percent frost chance.

Another U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp also said the longer-term outlook suggests cold temperatures during the weekend of August 9. But it said at this time it would rate any chance of damaging cold at less than 10 percent.
Brazil's independent meteorologist Somar said a cold front is forecast to reach southern Brazil but it was not likely to reach coffee areas and it was too early to predict frost.
So far, Brazil has escaped crop-damaging frost this winter. The last severe frosts were in 1994, one in late June and another in early July.
LIFFE's volume stood just 3,549 lots. Traders said there was also not much left to do on spot July, which goes off the board at lunchtime on Thursday.
The contract bucked the overall trend to end $3 down at $1,650.
The uncovered position on July fell 114 lots to 161 at the close of business on Tuesday.
In switches, Sept/Nov was traded at $8-$10.
